contributions.title: fix(flags): simplify readiness probe to prevent cascade failures
contributions.body:
## Problem

During high load, the `/_readiness` endpoint blocks on `pool.acquire()` for all 4 database pools. This can timeout and cause pods to be pulled from Kubernetes rotation—exactly when we need them most. This creates a cascade failure where busy pods are removed, increasing load on remaining pods.

Readiness should answer "can this pod serve traffic?" not "are all dependencies up?" During DB outages, keeping pods in rotation (returning fast errors) is better than removing them entirely.

contributions.body:
## Problem

During pool exhaustion bursts (e.g. Feb 24: 314K acquire timeouts/hour on `persons_reader`), the feature-flags service amplifies load instead of shedding it:

contributions.body:
## Problem

The toolbar OAuth redirect flow (introduced in #49579) fails on production because browsers and proxies percent-encode the `:` and `,` delimiters in the URL hash fragment (`%3A` and `%2C`). The frontend regex that extracts the authorization code never matches, so the code exchange silently fails and the toolbar params stay in the URL.

Additionally, the backend callback discards any original URL fragment (e.g. `#section1` from SPA routes), breaking hash-based routing for customers.

contributions.title: chore(personhog): gRPC connection churn tuning
contributions.body:
## Problem

The personhog Django client shows p95 latency of ~80ms while the service itself processes requests in ~5ms.
The root cause is gRPC channel churn: each Django worker process (Nginx Unit, 4 workers/pod, 30-200 pods) holds a singleton `PersonHogClient`, each worker's channel goes IDLE between requests. Every subsequent request pays the full reconnection cost. (DNS resolve + TCP connect + HTTP/2 handshake = ~60-80ms overhead).

Channel state transition  IDLE→CONNECTING rate matches

contributions.body:
## Problem

The Klime destination template gates **all** property/trait inclusion behind the `include_all_properties` boolean. When this is `false` (the default), three things break:

contributions.title: feat(experiments): throttle metric queries with rolling concurrency limit
contributions.body:
## Problem

Experiments fire all metric queries (sometimes up to 50) simultaneously via `Promise.all`. Each query goes through Celery's `process_query_task`, which has a per-team concurrency limit of 10 slots (Redis sorted set, no waiting queue). When all 50 hit at once, 40 get `ConcurrencyLimitExceeded` and enter a retry loop with exponential backoff. Meanwhile, the frontend's 606-second polling timeout ticks from when `pollForResults` starts - not from when Celery actually executes the query

contributions.title: fix(personhog): its always NODELAY
contributions.body:
## Problem

The personhog gRPC services (router and replica) show ~40-65ms of unexplained p99 tail latency on the router→replica hop. At p50, the hop adds ~0.1ms (normal), but at p99 it balloons to 40-65ms. This pattern is consistent with the interaction between Nagle's algorithm (sender buffers small writes until outstanding ACKs return) and TCP delayed ACKs (receiver waits up to 40ms before ACKing). When HTTP/2 frames a gRPC request as multiple small writes (HEADERS + DATA), Nagle holds back
contributions.author: nickbest-ph

contributions.author: robbie-c

contributions.title: feat(analytics-platform): emit cache-hit metric for lazy computation executions
contributions.body:
## Problem

The lazy computation framework only emits a structured `lazy_computation.executed` log line per invocation. ## Context

Once #57529 ships RFC 6750 \`insufficient_scope\` challenges and #57528 confirms client behavior, MCP no longer needs to publish its own \`scopes_supported\`. The AS becomes the single source of truth. Linear/Notion/Cloudflare/Stripe already ship without it.

This is the architecture from [Matt's #56835 review comment](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/56835#issuecomment-3567005020):
> Better fix is probably dropping scopes_supported from the resource metadata entirely. RFC 972

After #56835, the MCP server's published \`scopes_supported\` is generated from \`posthog/scopes.py\` at build time. This aligns the lists at commit time but they deploy independently:

- **MCP ahead of Django:** Worker advertises a scope AS rejects. Same \`invalid_scope\` bug, smaller window.

contributions.title: [Tracking] Eliminate OAuth scope-list drift across PostHog services
contributions.body:
## Context

PostHog has multiple parallel scope lists across services that must agree. Drift between any two breaks OAuth sign-in for spec-compliant clients with `?error=invalid_scope`.

Surfaces today:
1. `posthog/scopes.py` (canonical source)
2. AS metadata `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (computed from #1)
3. MCP protected-resource metadata `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (generated from #1 via #56835)
4. `ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_SCOPES` partner allowlist (hand-maintained)
5. W
